variants.title: One tenant dominates a shard
variants.context: A single tenant creates 70% of all writes, but the data is stored in one shard.
variants.constraint: The hottest user still produces a hotspot.
variants.question: What is the correct fix?
variants.expectedPattern: Repartition by tenant or key so the hotspot is spread across several shards.

variants.title: Hot key in a hash range
variants.context: One user or key is accessed far more than others, causing one shard to saturate.
variants.constraint: The shard assignment is not balanced enough.
variants.question: What pattern addresses the bottleneck?
variants.expectedPattern: A better sharding strategy or key distribution that avoids hotspots.

variants.title: Large user table under heavy writes
variants.context: An application table keeps growing and a single database shard eventually shows 95% CPU.
variants.constraint: The data is still concentrated in one partition.
variants.question: How do you reduce the hotspot?
variants.expectedPattern: Shard the table based on a stable key or tenant distribution.
wrongChoices: Keep a single DB and increase memory
Route all traffic to a queue

variants.title: Cross-shard fan-out gets expensive
variants.context: The app starts sharding by user but some requests need data from many shards at once.
variants.constraint: A common query now touches multiple partitions.
variants.question: What is the tradeoff?
variants.expectedPattern: Revisit the access pattern and keep hot data local to avoid heavy cross-shard queries.

variants.title: New tenant creates skew after launch
variants.context: A new customer becomes very active overnight and one shard absorbs most traffic.
variants.constraint: Static shard layout is not resilient to skew.
variants.question: What should happen?
variants.expectedPattern: Rebalance or re-shard before the hotspot becomes permanent.
wrongChoices: Add a cache as the only defense

variants.title: Orders table struggles under broad writes
variants.context: Millions of orders are stored in one table and write traffic is spread more evenly than expected, yet one shard is still overloaded.
variants.constraint: The partitioning key is poorly chosen.
variants.question: What design mistake caused it?
variants.expectedPattern: The key choice creates uneven distribution and a hotspot despite multiple shards.

variants.title: Heavy read and write imbalance
variants.context: One shard gets all the writes and the others sit mostly idle.
variants.constraint: The app is horizontally scaled but the data model is still skewed.
variants.question: What does the system need to do?
variants.expectedPattern: Improve partitioning strategy so the read and write workload is spread more evenly.

variants.title: Queueing data on same shard
variants.context: Every new order is placed on the same partition because the sharding key is not random enough.
variants.constraint: Data is not evenly distributed across consumers.
variants.question: What should be changed?
variants.expectedPattern: Choose a better sharding key or a consistent hashing strategy that spreads the load.
wrongChoices: Move the queue before the database

variants.title: Shard growth after customer expansion
variants.context: One business customer expands quickly and all of its data starts landing in the same shard.
variants.constraint: A large tenant becomes the data hotspot.
variants.question: How do you keep the system healthy?
variants.expectedPattern: Split that tenant’s data across multiple shards or use a more granular key distribution.
wrongChoices: Keep all of one tenant in a single partition

variants.title: Geo-based partition seems simple but fails
variants.context: Data is partitioned by region, but one region’s traffic is far higher than the others.
variants.constraint: The partition map is static and some regions are much hotter than the rest.
variants.question: What is the design flaw?
variants.expectedPattern: Hot regions still need a balance strategy; geography alone does not prevent skew.
wrongChoices: Hot regions should never be used

variants.title: Sharding by created_at
variants.context: New rows all land in this month’s partition while older partitions sit idle.
variants.constraint: Write load follows time, not a hash of the entity.
variants.question: Why is time a risky primary shard key?
variants.expectedPattern: Monotonic keys concentrate writes on the newest shard; hash or mix another high-cardinality key.
wrongChoices: Time-based keys always spread writes evenly
Add more old partitions to absorb new writes
Disable indexes on the new partition only

variants.title: Lookup without the shard key
variants.context: Support search is by email, but the table is sharded by user_id, so every query fans out.
variants.constraint: Email lookups are frequent.
variants.question: What restores single-shard lookups?
variants.expectedPattern: A lookup table or secondary index that maps email to the shard key.

variants.title: Resharding with downtime
variants.context: Moving 8 TB to new shards requires an 11-hour write freeze.
variants.constraint: The product cannot take that outage.
variants.question: What operational pattern splits data live?
variants.expectedPattern: Dual-write or consistent-hash migration with incremental copy and cutover, not a long freeze.
wrongChoices: mysqldump and restore during business hours
Change the shard count without moving data

variants.title: UUID v1 hotspot
variants.context: Shard key is a time-ordered UUID and inserts hammer one range.
variants.constraint: IDs look random but are sequential in practice.
variants.question: What key property do you need?
variants.expectedPattern: High-cardinality keys that hash uniformly, not monotonically increasing identifiers.
wrongChoices: Auto-increment integers as the shard key

variants.title: Multi-tenant report across shards
variants.context: A global admin report joins every tenant’s orders by scanning all shards.
variants.constraint: The report is rare; tenant dashboards are the hot path.
variants.question: How do you keep tenant traffic fast?
variants.expectedPattern: Keep tenant queries single-shard; run global reports asynchronously on a warehouse or scatter-gather off the hot path.
wrongChoices: Make every tenant query scan all shards
Put all tenants back on one node for reports
Lock all shards during the admin report

variants.title: Chat rooms on one partition
variants.context: Messages are sharded by room_id and a viral room saturates one disk.
variants.constraint: A single room can exceed one shard’s write capacity.
variants.question: How do you split a hot room?
variants.expectedPattern: Sub-partition the hot key (room plus time or hash buckets) so one room can span shards.
wrongChoices: Keep the whole room on one shard forever
Move only reads to another shard

variants.title: Foreign keys across shards
variants.context: Orders live on shard A and users on shard B, so a foreign key cannot be enforced by the database.
variants.constraint: Referential integrity is now an application concern.
variants.question: What design follows from sharding?
variants.expectedPattern: Drop cross-shard FKs; enforce relationships in the app or keep related data on the same shard.
wrongChoices: Expect the database to enforce cross-shard FKs
Duplicate every user onto every order shard without a key
Use a single global lock for all inserts

variants.title: Modulo N and adding a shard
variants.context: Keys are user_id % 4; adding a fifth shard would remap almost every row.
variants.constraint: Resharding must move as little data as possible.
variants.question: Which mapping reduces churn?
variants.expectedPattern: Consistent hashing (or range maps) so most keys stay put when capacity is added.
wrongChoices: user_id % N with N changing freely
One new shard that receives all old data

variants.title: Secondary index imbalance
variants.context: Data is well sharded by user_id, but a global unique username index still lives on one node.
variants.constraint: Username checks are write-heavy at signup.
variants.question: Where is the remaining hotspot?
variants.expectedPattern: The global unique index must also be partitioned or moved to a dedicated lookup service.
wrongChoices: Ignore the index because the table is sharded
Put usernames in app memory only

variants.title: Directory service stale map
variants.context: A shard map says user 42 is on shard 3, but the row was migrated to shard 7.
variants.constraint: Clients cache the directory for 10 minutes.
variants.question: What keeps routing correct during moves?
variants.expectedPattern: Versioned shard maps, short cache, and a forwarding hint from the old shard.
wrongChoices: Delete the row from both shards during migration
